title: Supported sections and flasque objects
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $s:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the complementary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Fix a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$ (in particular the finite ring $A_{E,n}$ fixed by [def-pur-conventions]). Work in the abelian categories of all sheaves of modules over the constant coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with the identified coefficient inverse images [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. No constructibility condition is imposed on these sheaves. Write $j^*,s^{-1}$ for the underived module inverse images and $j_*,s_*$ for the underived direct images.

Let $\eta_{j,M}:M\to j_*j^*M$ be the unit of $j^*\dashv j_*$. Define the sheaf of sections supported on $Z$ by
$$
 \mathcal G_ZM=\ker(\eta_{j,M}).
$$
Explicitly, for an object $V\to X$ of the site,
$$
 (\mathcal G_ZM)(V)=\{m\in M(V):m|_{V\times_XU}=0\}.
$$
Its restriction maps are those of $M$. On a morphism $f:M\to N$, use the restriction of $f$ to these kernels; naturality of $\eta_j$ makes this a functor. Define
$$
 s^!M=s^{-1}\mathcal G_ZM,
$$
and on morphisms use $s^{-1}(\mathcal G_Zf)$. This is exactly the sheaf construction $s^!_0$ of [def-exc-proetale-sections-with-support]. The functors $\mathcal G_Z$ and $s^!$ are left exact. The notation $s^!$ denotes the closed inverse image of the supported kernel; it may coincide with ordinary restriction $s^{-1}$ for particular pairs, for example $Z=X$.

If $j$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], the canonical unit of the closed inverse-image/direct-image adjunction gives a natural isomorphism
$$
 \mathcal G_ZM\xrightarrow{\sim}s_*s^!M.
$$
Thus in that case $\mathcal G_ZM$ is the closed direct image of the indicated sheaf on $Z$. For an arbitrary complementary open immersion this canonical comparison need not be an isomorphism, even with a nonzero finite coefficient ring and an affine base scheme.

A sheaf $I$ is called *flasque for this pair* if the unit $\eta_{j,I}:I\to j_*j^*I$ is an epimorphism in the abelian category of module sheaves, equivalently if its sheaf cokernel is zero. This is the pair-specific condition, with no assertion that the map on sections over every object is surjective.

proof.text: Evaluate the functor-category kernel at the sheaf M and site object V. Evaluation preserves kernels; ShortComplex.kernelSequence and moduleCat_range_eq_ker identify the sectionwise inclusion with the kernel of the open adjunction unit. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies that actual unit with restriction under upperStarIsoOpenImmersionRestriction. Injectivity of the comparison isomorphism identifies the two zero loci.

proof.text: The supported-kernel functor is the limit of the parallel pair of the identity and j inverse-image/direct-image composite, both left exact. limitIsoFlipCompLim and pointwise finite-limit preservation give left exactness. Compose with the exact closed inverse image for finiteClosedUpperShriek.

proof.text: The triangle identity makes the image under j inverse image of the open unit a split monomorphism. Exact inverse image carries its kernel to zero. Apply isIso_upperStarLowerStarAdjunction_unit_app_of_isCompl to this supported kernel; its quasi-compact-complement hypothesis is the one in the statement. Naturality upgrades component isomorphisms to an isomorphism of functors.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Preadditive.epi_iff_isZero_cokernel to the open unit. This is sheaf epimorphy and the sheaf cokernel, with no sectionwise surjectivity claim.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian; epimorphism criterion and the two identity/empty-complement calculations

proof.text: Apply lem-pur-infinite-clopen-pair with k = ULift (ZMod 2) and I = ULift Nat. On each nonempty coordinate clopen use the rank-one sheaf of continuous functions into the discrete ring Lambda, and push it forward to X. The fpqc sheaf theorem for continuous functions proves the sheaf condition. Form c: coproduct H_i → product H_i and M = cokernel c.

source.place: def-pur-flasque-support, step 5: infinite product of fields, coordinate clopens and their closed complement.

proof.text: If c were epic it would be locally surjective. A sheaf colimit is the sheafification of its presheaf colimit: the sheafification adjunction identifies the colimit comparison with the unit followed by an isomorphism. Express the coproduct as a filtered colimit of finite subcoproducts. Local representatives of the tuple of ones therefore have finite supports. Use only finite_cover_refinement from the affine-evaluation module: a finite cover makes the union of those supports finite. Choose a missing coordinate. Its section of ones restricts to zero on this cover, so separatedness makes it zero globally, contrary to nonemptiness of the coordinate piece and nontriviality of Lambda. Hence c is not epic and M is nonzero.

source.place: def-pur-flasque-support, step 5: infinite product of fields, coordinate clopens and their closed complement.

proof.text: Each closed pullback of H_i is zero: pushforward from a clopen equals extension by zero, which vanishes after pullback to the disjoint closed complement. Forgetting scalar structure compares the fixed-module inverse image with set inverse image. The forgetful comparison and immersion limit-preservation theorem show that closed inverse image preserves the product; it therefore kills the product and its cokernel M. On a coordinate clopen all other H_i vanish. The map c there is split epic by the surviving-coordinate insertion and projection, so its cokernel vanishes. Localization conservativity for the coordinate open cover implies j inverse-image M = 0.

source.place: def-pur-flasque-support, step 5: infinite product of fields, coordinate clopens and their closed complement.

proof.text: Since j inverse-image M = 0, the supported kernel of M is isomorphic to M, using the kernel of the zero unit. Its closed inverse image is zero, so the comparison has nonzero source and zero target and cannot be an isomorphism. Assemble this with the affine pair, closed/open immersions, complementary ranges, and non-quasi-compact open inclusion.

source.place: def-pur-flasque-support, step 5: infinite product of fields, coordinate clopens and their closed complement.
